answer: Attention-Duration Claim. A new identity must hold a continuously sampled attention task—responding to unpredictable probes—for a long karst-like accumulation period before its votes count. The rule sets a trellis of checkpoints: each probe missed resets accrued duration. An attacker running N duplicates must supply N sustained live operators, so the per-identity cost is real human attention over time, not a one-time payment. Growth is capped by the herd's ridge of genuinely watchable hours per day.
